translation: Guijiao (tortoise shell glue, stir-fried with clam powder into pearls), Lujiaojiao (deer antler glue, stir-fried with clam powder into pearls), Hujinggu (tiger shin bone, roasted with butter), Heshouwu (Polygonum multiflorum, mixed with black beans, steamed and sun-dried nine times each), Chuanniuxi (Achyranthes, washed in wine and dried in the sun), Duzhong (Eucommia, stir-fried with ginger juice until the threads break), Suoyang (Cynomorium), Danggui (Angelica, washed in wine, stir-fried and dried, two liang each), Weilingxian (Clematis, washed in wine), Huangbai (Phellodendron, washed in wine and dried in the sun, stir-fried in wine with a little salt), Renshen (ginseng, root hairs removed), Qianghuo (Notopterygium), Ganjiang (dried ginger), Baishaoyao (white peony, slightly stir-fried), Yunbaizhu (Atractylodes macrocephala, stir-fried with earth, one liang each), Shudihuang (cooked Rehmannia, three liang), Chuanfuzi (large Sichuan aconite, with one bowl each of boy's urine and salt water, and two liang of fresh ginger; slice and boil together for a whole day until extremely cooked, when the water dries add more, after boiling in the salt water take it out, peel and cut into thin slices, then change to clean water, add five qian of Chuan Huanglian and five qian of Gancao, boil together for the length of three incense sticks, take out and dry in the sun, only use when it is bright like amber, one liang five qian). Grind all together into a fine powder, refine honey into pills the size of wutong seeds (梧桐子), take three qian each time, on an empty stomach with light salt water; in winter take with light yellow wine. <ins>Haitongpi Tang</ins> (Erythrina Bark Decoction, 海桐皮湯) (seen in the injury of the two cheekbones) <ins>Dingtong San</ins> (Pain-Relieving Powder, 定痛散) (seen in the injury of the shanjiao bone).
